So linking via the extracted libc.so script would fail to find libc_nonshared.a because it's an absolute path in the script. Options:
- Patch the extracted libc.so linker script to point to the sysroot absolute path.
- Or create the symlink in the sysroot and use `-L sysroot` — but the GROUP absolute paths override search dirs.

Actually the linker script has absolute paths, so it'll look at /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc_nonshared.a which doesn't exist. We can either copy libc_nonshared.a to a path we can write (no) or patch the script. We can edit the extracted copy's libc.so to use relative/sysroot paths. Since we extracted to /tmp/sysroot (or $HOME/sysroot), we can rewrite those absolute paths.

Simplest: replace `/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6` with the actual absolute path (exists on system, fine — no need to change) and `/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc_nonshared.a` with `/tmp/sysroot/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc_nonshared.a`.

SYS="$HOME/.local/rust-gnu-sysroot/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu"
GCC="$HOME/.local/rust-gnu-sysroot/usr/lib/gcc/aarch64-linux-gnu/12"

pie=0
